quantisation_bound: 5 mm per axis (1 cm position quantum, round-to-nearest); Euclidean <= 8.7 mm; exact against the quantised truth at every delivered tick
notes: The emitter owns the canon (10,000 seeded objects: random walks, circular orbits and a few fast movers) and a 10 m spatial hash, and it is viewpoint-agnostic: it knows each subscriber's interest region, not its camera. At every delivery it intersects the subscriber's moving region (a sphere or a perspective frustum) with the hash and sends only the difference from what that subscriber already holds: objects that entered the region (absolute quantised pose), objects that left (id only), and objects whose pose moved (a quantised delta). The pose delta is measured against what the projector can *predict* from the motion channel it already holds - a snapshot of position, velocity and time, extrapolated - so an object moving smoothly costs nothing at all, and the projector applies the identical prediction, so the two agree exactly. Positions are quantised to a 1 cm grid (round-to-nearest): a reconstruction is off by at most 5 mm per axis (8.7 mm Euclidean) and never drifts, because every delta is taken against the quantised truth, never against an accumulated estimate. Deltas travel as biased fixed-width bit fields, one 64-bit word per object, whose width is chosen per axis to minimise the total cost (width times objects plus the escapes); outliers that do not fit escape into a varint list, so a few fast movers cannot widen the field for everybody else. The changed set travels as a bitmap over the subscriber's previous set whenever that is smaller than the id list. The motion channel carries each object's velocity in 1/64 quantum per tick in world coordinates; the projector converts it into its own frame (and into optical flow) locally, which is what lets it interpolate between deliveries. Every packet carries since_version, so a late joiner or a subscriber that lost a packet is detected and resynchronised from a keyframe (the full region with absolute poses), after which it rebuilds the emitter's ground truth exactly. The emitter is single threaded and serves the 64 subscribers on their own cadences (2-60 Hz, staggered, so the load per tick is even); 9471363 delivered states were compared against the ground truth and 0 mismatched.
